chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) who said:

The slave (male or female) is not validly divorced nor validly married except by the permission of his master. I said: If the master had married him/her, to whom does the right of divorce belong? He said: To the master. God gave an example: a slave who has no power over anything. The 'anything' refers to divorce.

key_terms.اَلْمَمْلُوكُ: The slave (male or female), referring to a person owned as property under classical fiqh
key_terms.بِإِذْنِ سَيِّدِهِ: By the permission of his master
key_terms.بِيَدِ: In the hand of (meaning under the authority of)

ai.seo_question: Who has the authority to divorce a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic principle that a slave’s marital status is an extension of the master’s property rights, meaning the master retains the exclusive authority to dissolve the union even if he initiated the marriage. The Imam’s reference to the Quranic verse regarding a 'slave whom you cannot control' underscores the theological basis for this lack of independent legal agency (istikhlaf) in personal status matters. This ruling highlights the distinct legal capacity of slaves compared to free persons in classical Shia fiqh.
